name: Bell Sixlimb
description: Tolk's species: cat-sized, six-limbed, four-handed, from the terminator band of a TRAPPIST-1 world. Wild, not made. Their cells keep a written payload for a lifetime, which is the same strangeness that lets a human child open a door.
narrative:
Invented life, placed under the constraint in the gm-secret notes: the terminator
band of a tidally-locked TRAPPIST-1 world is a real environment with real
perpetual wind and a real survivable temperature ring, and nobody has observed
its surface.

Sixlimbs brachiate, nest in wind-shadow, and are social in groups of five to
nine. They acquire language -- actual syntax, not mimicry -- from whoever is
around.

And their cells hold what is written into them, perfectly, for life. Which is
the same impossible housekeeping a first-through's body performs on the damage a
crossing does. Two species, forty light years apart, no common ancestor.

Nobody engineered this. That is the part that keeps people awake.

extras.the_correspondence: Keeping and opening are halves of one phenomenon. A sixlimb cannot cross alone; a first-through cannot hold a payload.

actor_notes: Not a monster and not a pet. If a GM needs a fetch sixlimb, this is it. Never fight these as adversaries -- they are a people, and the campaign's one firm line about them is that nobody in it treats them as fauna without being wrong.
